It was an exercise in walking, essentially. I'm sure if I were really into swords or something I'd find a reason to go to the sword museum specifically. But unless you have a very particular interest, museums < Internet.

I think its worth while to see an artifact up close, but maybe it isn't worth occupying large real estate in the center of a city. I think the national science museums which are more kid focused rather than art do what they're intended to do well. Being the anarchist I am I don't think government should be funding that but the idea of a building holding interesting things that can entertain and teach kids works.
A privately owned museum could probably afford more artifacts and a better plot of land. Walking up 8 flights of stairs just to see some shit is really annoying.

Physical items are much harder to change the narrative with. Aftifact curation. You can have a folder of saved images, and files related; whole databases. But you need the physical artifact for people to see, to know, to remember the history of. My friend has long since forgiven me for stealing his pumpkin, though I didn't tell him who the culprit was until after the funeral in the swamp.
